sentences.text: This appeal under Section 14(A) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against the order dated 18.07.2023 passed by Special Judge SC/ST(PA) Indore, in Bail application No.2620/2023 whereby learned Special Judge rejected the bail application of appellant.
He is in detention since 09.07.2023.
3. As per the prosecution story, the allegations against the appellant is that he has committed rape upon prosecutrix of marriage.
4 . Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant is innocent and has not committed any offence.
It is further submitted that the applicant has been implicated in the present case.
The prosecutrix is a 27 years old lady.
The appellant is in jail since 09.07.2023.
Final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant/accused be released on bail, pending the trial.

5 . Learned counsel for the objector has opposed the prayer and submitted that the appellant has made physical relationship with the prosecutrix for 1 and half year and used abuse language regarding caste, hence, the benefit of grant of bail to the appellant be not granted.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed for grant of bail and prayed for rejection of the application.

7. Having taken into consideration all the fact and circumstances of the case and custody period of the appellant, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant/accused is not warranted.

Consequently,
appeal stands allowed.

8. It is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE Vindesh Kaustubh @ Chikoo Bhattacharya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190272517/
